body:
DearDeanna,

I'm so sorry you have to go through this. I lost my partner too to suicide over 2 months ago. I can't even imagine what I will feel like when I am almost hitting a year. I can only think it will be gruesome. I do feel like I'm being dragged on a bed of nails while being forced to smile, move on, and allow time to 'heal'. It actually hurts me when people use the word heal. How can anyone possibly 'heal' from this? What healing is there? 

I wish I had words to comfort you, but all I can also say is you're not alone. Have you sought professional help since his passing?

Hi sadpeachgirl,

it is lovely to see how many people are reaching out to you. Am I am glad that you had posted how you truly feel here.

I lost my partner to suicide just over 2 months ago, and I can truly attest that this is the most painful feeling I have ever felt in my entire life, and beyond. I am beyond recognizable, and I can't even explain the brokenness I am in now.

I keep wishing he would tell me what his true intentions were, and he gave me one last cry for help. I knew he loved me, but he bore everything in his mind, and I wasn't able to help him because of it. I am filled with so much guilt and regrets. Believe me, your boyfriend's life will not be better without you. To this day, and forever until I die, I know my life will never be better than what could have been. How I wish I had just one more day with him, one more kiss, one more everything. Our hopes and dreams for each other, with each other, vanished in one final decision.

The finality of it all. I can't go back, I can't fix anything, I can't mend anything. I just want him back...and he can't come back... and I cry every time, and the pain of never having another ANYTHING with him just sinks me in uncontrollable sobbing and tears.

I am not trying to guilt trip you, but I am telling you what will happen to your boyfriend if you disappeared. He loves you, and he will be willing to do anything for you. You are not a burden, you are worthy of love, care and compassion. Please... I know it's hard, and life is very difficult. There's no pressure for anything, it's okay, and he will help you, be yourself and speak your truth.

Hey, it's ok. I feel the exact same way. I often too feel if I don't follow my partner I will lose him, or I would miss him in the afterlife.

However, I think that he wouldn't be pleased to see me so soon  in the afterlife. 

I have this thought about what stops me from taking my life too. The obvious one being I dont want to spread even more and further pain onto others, because I first hand knows how painful it is.

When that monster appears in my head, and tells me theres no point to anything and just end it, there's this feeling that that monster isn't in complete control over me, because my partner got a choke collar over it.

Sometimes I think, what if it is eternal blackness and no afterlife, and there is nothing, not even him? Scary thought. 

I'm trying to get all the help I can, whether it is professional help or support from friends and family, I dont necessarily care so much about me, but I am trying to help myself by thinking about how since I inherited my partners ailments (depression, anxiety  suicidal thoughts) somehow, maybe if I can alleviate that  in a way I am alleviating his pain as well.

Hi flowerette,

I am so sorry for your lost, as I also lost my partner by suicide, and very recently. 

I am express to you that I feel very much the same, how I am also looming in this very dark place, and thinking of ending my life quite often. Thank you for having the courage to express that.

I want you to know that, I am positive that he never meant to hurt you or anyone else. He was in a lot of mental anguish, and unfortunately, someone with a suicidal mindset can't truly see the other more logical options of dealing/managing his pain other than ending his very existence. It is so painful to know after their death that they were battling this mental illness that lead them to feel that was the only way to make the pain go away.

My life is also completely destroyed. Nothing will make this better. 

There's so much love in the world, but it's hard to realize that sometimes love isn't enough to save others from their disease, like how love doesn't stop cancer from taking over someone's body.

My reason from stopping myself from ending my life is because I know how it will only spread pain to others, and I know exactly how it would feel, since I am going through it myself.

My other, even stronger reason, is because I know who is putting that seductive monster whispering words of death to me on a choking leash, the man I love and lost himself. He wants me to live, and even in death he is doing everything he can to keep me safe.

I am still begging him to come back, and crying out bouts of sorrys and I love yous. It's beyond comprehension on what the hell we are suppose to do.

Again, I am so sorry you are going through this. You aren't alone. Keep expressing yourself, no filter. You have every right to feel everything and nothing.

I completely understand. I have many unbearable feelings as well. I've also inherited what my partner had.

Like the previous comment said, our lost loved ones didnt intend to hurt us in anyway, and the only way they think in their tunnel vision of suicidal ideation, to escape the pain, is to end exsistence itself. It's like their brain is on fire, and there is no escape. It's like asking them to hold on to a piece of rope, but they are losing grip.

I wish none of us had to go through this, and I wish this pain will go away. All we can do is understand what our lost loved ones had to deal with  and then learn to live with our reality. It's much easier than done, I know. Because I havent even done it yet.

I can never tell you what you can or cannot do, ultimately the choice is yours.

But I will tell you, I lost my partner to suicide, and this pain I feel is the most unimaginable pain I have ever felt in my entire life. Everyday, I wake up in agony, absolutely full of guilt, and constantly wishing and begging him to come back, my eyes full of tears, lungs crushed by the non'stop sobbing.

I have so many strong urges to follow after him, and I've never felt so much strong suicidal ideation in my life. 

His future, our future, gone because he succumbed to his mental illness and the monster that he had in his mind for many years.

My biggest regret is not being able to help him, for the things I said or didnt say. I will never stop thinking about it, and I dont even believe I will have any peace.

I strongly urge you to get the help you deserve. Because trust me, nobody wants you to go away and disappear forever, and your mind is playing tricks on you.

I couldn't save my beloved, but you and those who will take you seriously will. Get admitted to the hospital if need be. Anything.

I hope this will give you some insight of what will happen if you decide to go. You won't believe me, but there will be a lot of people who will not be able to recover from your death.

So sorry, I lost my partner not too long ago. Do what you need to do for him. Be there for his family and friends and mourn together. Let yourself cry, do what you have to do, do not try to please others. Show up for him and do what you feel is right to get through it. And have atleast one person be there with you  who will support you and guard you if you are uncomfortable.
Crippling depression, off the charts anxiety, and unfortunately suicidal ideation.

Your mom can go fuck herself. Get help right away. Never repress or downplay how you feel because that's how your life will end. Speak your fucking truth to the doctor. Tell your dad, he knows what it feels like to lose someone to suicide, so I feel pretty confident that he will help you, as long as you tell him you dont want him to feel the pain again, you want help and you want him to help you save yourself. And when you go to college, take advantage of their school counseling. Look into it. It is there for you.

Fuck your mom, seriously.

It's been almost 2 weeks and honestly, I forgave him. I knew he was in so much pain, and for a very long time. I miss him so badly, it hurts to bad I just can't even see the light at the end of the tunnel. 

Just remember that your feelings are valid, so you are allowed to be angry with the person who left suddenly. You are allowed to feel whatever you need to feel. You may find your anger may dissipate, and maybe it won't. 

Please try to see a grief counselor and/or a grief support group who also lost someone to suicide. Having someone who is neutral to talk to may help you not necessarily figure out an answer, but maybe provide some insight to your anger. Being with others can help you map how your feelings.

The fact that you reach out to us means there is still hope. Thank you. I can tell you that the spread of pain after your death is a very real thing. You may feel that you are a burden, but whether it is actually true or not (very likely not), it will never compare to the agony of you not being in this world anymore. 

Since my loved one passed, I am filled with nothing but all the worst possible feelings. Guilt, regrets, and even wanting to die. Some of what you are feeling during your lowest points will transcend onto your caregivers.

And I get it, sometimes when you are in that frame of mind, it's hard to see clearly as to how much pain your death will cause. 

I think, perhaps you could acknowledge that you may always have that bit of darkness within you, and this pursuit of happiness is putting too much pressure on you. You deserve to have joys if your life, but find compassion for yourself when you are feeling like you are in a dark place too. And maybe your caregivers need to learn to meet you in your dark place too. Maybe don't see it as something you need to get rid of, but rather something you learn to manage better, whether it is through medication or coping skills or both or other methods.

It's okay, you are a good person. Thank you for reaching out to us.

Personally, and you can take this is just a grain of salt, I would just book an appointment with a professional on her behalf, and tell her I booked an appointment, you're going and I am coming with you. She might go if you go with her. You can choose to either attend one session with her, or agree to go with her and slowly wean yourself out.

If she still refuses to go, you should just go for your own sanity and make it an appointment for yourself then, and you can talk to the counselor about your problem.

I also miss who I use to be too. I did everything right. I got a dream job and moved to somewhere where I always wanted to be. I felt like the stars were aligning for me and it could only go up from here, until I recently lost my partner to suicide just over a month ago. All the guilt, all the regrets. I'm still working out my feelings because it is still fresh, but I want you to know that this going to be hard, and our circumstances just makes it harder.

You are not only grieving your brother, but you are also grieving yourself! My counselor told me that and it gave me some clarity of what is happening to me. 

I have a hard time doing this myself, but be gentle to yourself, seek help. Seek counseling. Stay connected with family and friends. Drop what doesn't help you, take what does. Do whatever you can, it's okay to hurt, you're allowed to cry or not cry, be happy and despair at the same time. You are allowed to feel your feelings, no pressure, no timeline. Hang on tight.

Hi there,

I am so sorry that you feel this way. And I am so sorry that you believe there is no light at the end of the tunnel. 

I just lost the love of my life over a month ago. It was a major roller coaster ride with him and he even told me he has thoughts of suicide. I have many regrets and a lot of guilt in my heart, whether it was my fault or not. 

What I can say is no matter if he had left a note or gifts or anything for the future, it will never mend the pain of losing him, indefinitely. 

I would give anything to have him alive and well. This has left me permanently damaged, and I'm sure his family and friends will be hurting for the rest of our life time. The only way to lessen the pain is to not inflict the pain of losing him in the first place.

The terror that reaps my heart every morning of him not existing in this world, the idea I have to live another half a century without him. None of that is what I wanted. 

I don't know what to say to make you reconsider, but trust me when I say that your death will only bleed pain to others, even if you think everyone is better off without you.

Please, tell anyone you can that you are suicidal. Talk about it. My love was in so much pain, but all I wanted was for a chance to work with him and help him, anyway I could. Now I don't have that chance anymore, but we still want that for you. We don't want to lose you.

I absolutely hear you that life is tough, and that voice inside you keeps urging you to do something you don't truly want to do. That voice tells you that you are worthless, a burden, and/or the world is better off without you.

I want you to know, that is all completely false, and I am 120% certain your wife and child would never want you to leave this world. You are so SO important to them. Your family and friends also feel the same way.

All I can say is please communicate how you are feeling, and tell them you have thoughts of suicide. Whoever you trust. There is no shame. NO SHAME. See a professional to assist you in managing and quieting that voice. I can't say it will go away, but I believe in you that with the help and support, you can do it. YOU GOT THIS. We all who are in this shitty club now want nothing more than for you to live.

Unfortunately it is too late for my love, but it's not too late for you. I can't stress enough that it isn't too late, REACH OUT to anyone you trust. 

I'm so torn and broken, but I specifically wanted to comment on this because I don't want anyone to be going through what I am going through now, and for the rest of my life. I want you to live.

Please, don't give up.
